attack_surfaces.operation: CALL rdx (indirect call to attacker-controlled RWX page)
attack_surfaces.reason: Attacker supplies up to 0x1000 bytes of shellcode into an RWX mmap page, which is then executed via 'call rdx'. This is arbitrary code execution within the seccomp sandbox.

Seccomp sandbox uses SCMP_ACT_KILL_PROCESS default (deny-all) but whitelists open(2), clone(56), fork(57), vfork(58), execve(59), creat(85), execveat(322). Critically, read(0)/write(1)/sendto/sendfile are NOT whitelisted — shellcode cannot directly output data via standard I/O syscalls. The challenge is exfiltrating /flag.txt content without write/sendto. open+execve/execveat are available.

RWX page provides shellcode execution surface; combined with seccomp this is the intended sandbox-escape challenge. SHSTK+IBT (CET) enabled but mmap'd page is non-CET-marked shellcode — endbr64 not required for indirect call target since it's data page.
No RPATH/RUNPATH in binary; libseccomp.so.2 resolved from system path /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/. LD_LIBRARY_PATH would take precedence if set, but this is standard behavior, not a vulnerability.

facts.description: Binary is x86-64 PIE, dynamically linked, not stripped, compiled with GCC 9.3.0, source file sandbox.c
Security: Full RELRO, NX enabled, PIE enabled, No canary, SHSTK+IBT (CET) enabled
main() calls mmap(0, 0x1000, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC=7, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS=0x22, -1, 0) allocating an RWX page
main() prints two banner strings then calls bamAll() to install seccomp sandbox BEFORE reading user input
main() reads exactly 0x1000 bytes from stdin into the RWX mmap buffer in a loop (accumulates until offset==0x1000)
main() executes the buffer via 'call rdx' (rdx = mmap buffer pointer) after 0x1000 bytes received — arbitrary shellcode execution
bamAll() calls seccomp_init(0x7fff0000) = SCMP_ACT_KILL_PROCESS — default action kills process on any non-whitelisted syscall
bamAll() calls seccomp_arch_add(ctx, 0xc000003e) = AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64 to restrict to x86_64 syscalls only
bam(sysno) calls seccomp_rule_add(ctx, 0=SCMP_ACT_ALLOW, sysno, 0) — adds ALLOW rule for the given syscall
Whitelisted syscalls: open(2), clone(56), fork(57), vfork(58), execve(59), creat(85), execveat(322)
read(0), write(1), sendto(44), sendfile(40), sendmsg(46) are NOT in whitelist — shellcode cannot perform standard I/O output after seccomp_load
Banner strings: 'We always respect freedom of the press. You can write anything but you can only see what we want you to see.' and 'What you may want is located at /flag.txt, but you can\'t open it.'
Global variable ctx @ 0x4020 (.bss, 8 bytes) stores seccomp filter context pointer
libseccomp.so.2 v2.5.5 resolved from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libseccomp.so.2; no RPATH/RUNPATH in binary
mmap return value is stored in [rbp-0x8] but never checked against MAP_FAILED before use
The indirect call 'call rdx' at 0x1414 targets the mmap'd RWX page containing user input — this is the shellcode execution point
The seccomp policy is installed (seccomp_load) before read() — shellcode runs under full seccomp restriction
CET (SHSTK+IBT) is enabled in ELF notes, but the shellcode page is mmap'd data (not CET-marked); 'call rdx' is an indirect call to a non-ENDBR target
